chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Husayn ibn Hazim, from Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who consults his brother, but he is not sincere with him with a sincere opinion, Allah Mighty and Majestic would Confiscate his opinion.

key_terms.يَمْحَضْهُ: he is sincere with him / offers purely

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of insincere advice in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores that *shura* (consultation) is not merely a social courtesy but a spiritual transaction requiring *ikhlas* (sincerity) and *mahd al-ra'y* (unadulterated judgment). It serves as a divine warning that withholding one's true counsel out of hypocrisy or partiality results in the forfeiture of one's own intellectual and spiritual clarity, linking the quality of advice given to the quality of judgment received.
